app.name: Snapshot PB app
app.summary: The Snapshot PB app reads and writes the settings of a board through Bluetooth. It runs on Android, on Wear OS, on iOS, on the desktop, and in a browser.

wear.name: Wear OS
wear.description: The watch app shows the profiles and the fire mode. It does not edit the timing.

device_config.active_profile.title: Active profile
device_config.active_profile.description: The device screen shows the active profile under the name of the board. Select a profile in the list to make it active.

device_config.language.title: Language
device_config.language.description: The app does not change the language of the board. Set the language on the board.

autococker.fire_mode.title: Fire Mode
autococker.fire_mode.description: The fire mode of the profile. The app shows the modes that the board reports. A mode that the app does not know shows as Unknown.

wear.description: The watch app shows the fire mode and lets you select another one.

profile.fire_rate_cap.title: Fire Rate Cap
profile.fire_rate_cap.description: The maximum fire rate in balls per second. The cocking solenoid closed dwell increases when the fire rate is lower than the timing cycle permits. The app does not send 0, which the board reads as no cap.
profile.fire_rate_cap.where: Profile > Basic Function > Fire Rate Cap

autococker.eye_mode.title: Eye Mode
autococker.eye_mode.description: The type of eye that the marker has, if any.

autococker.eye_threshold.title: Eye Threshold
autococker.eye_threshold.description: The eye threshold as 0 to 100 percent of full scale. The eye sees a ball when the reading is below it. The app does not send 0, because the board would use its 50 percent default.

autococker.eye_debounce.title: Eye Debounce
autococker.eye_debounce.description: The time in milliseconds, in steps of 0.1 ms, that the eye must see a ball before the board accepts it.

autococker.sear_solenoid_dwell.title: Sear Solenoid Dwell
autococker.sear_solenoid_dwell.description: The time in milliseconds, in steps of 0.1 ms, that the sear solenoid is energized in the firing cycle. The Timing Overview diagram shows it in one cycle.

autococker.cocking_solenoid_delay.title: Cocking Solenoid Delay
autococker.cocking_solenoid_delay.description: The time in milliseconds, in steps of 0.1 ms, that the cocking solenoid waits after a trigger pull before it energizes.

autococker.cocking_solenoid_dwell_open.title: Cocking Solenoid Dwell Open
autococker.cocking_solenoid_dwell_open.description: The time in milliseconds, in steps of 0.1 ms, that the cocking solenoid energizes to open the breech. With an eye, the board ignores this setting.
autococker.cocking_solenoid_dwell_open.where: Profile > Timing > Cocking Solenoid Dwell Open

autococker.cocking_solenoid_dwell_closed.title: Cocking Solenoid Dwell Closed
autococker.cocking_solenoid_dwell_closed.description: The time in milliseconds, in steps of 0.1 ms, that the cocking solenoid stays de-energized to close the breech before the next cycle.
autococker.cocking_solenoid_dwell_closed.where: Profile > Timing > Cocking Solenoid Dwell Closed

autococker.cocking_solenoid_timeout.title: Cocking Solenoid Timeout
autococker.cocking_solenoid_timeout.description: The longest time in milliseconds, in steps of 0.1 ms, that the cocking solenoid waits for the eye before it closes on timing. The app always sends a value, so the timeout is never off.

autococker.trigger_debounce_on.title: Trigger Debounce On
autococker.trigger_debounce_on.description: The time in milliseconds, in steps of 0.1 ms, that the trigger must stay pulled to start a firing cycle.

autococker.trigger_debounce_off.title: Trigger Debounce Off
autococker.trigger_debounce_off.description: The time in milliseconds, in steps of 0.1 ms, that the trigger must stay released before the next pull counts.

autococker.ramping_custom_multiplier.title: Ramping Custom Multiplier
autococker.ramping_custom_multiplier.description: The fire rate in ramping, as a multiple of the trigger pull rate, after the pull threshold is met. For example, 2.5 with 3 pulls in one second gives 7.5 balls per second.

autococker.ramping_custom_trigger_pulls.title: Ramping Custom Trigger Pulls
autococker.ramping_custom_trigger_pulls.description: The number of trigger pulls in a one second window that starts ramping for the next second.
autococker.ramping_custom_trigger_pulls.where: Profile > Ramping > Ramping Custom Trigger Pulls

autococker.ramping_custom_rof_minimum.title: Ramping Custom ROF Minimum
autococker.ramping_custom_rof_minimum.description: The minimum rate of fire in ramping, whatever the number of trigger pulls in the window.
autococker.ramping_custom_rof_minimum.where: Profile > Ramping > Ramping Custom ROF Minimum

profile.board_auto_off.title: Board Auto Off
profile.board_auto_off.description: The time in minutes after the last trigger pull or button press at which the board turns off. The value 0 keeps the board on.
profile.board_auto_off.where: Profile > Basic Function > Board Auto Off

topic.bluetooth.title: Connect to a board
topic.bluetooth.description: Turn the Bluetooth radio of the board on. Open the Devices screen. The app lists the boards in range under Discovered Devices. Tap a board to connect to it.

wear.description: The watch app connects to the board that the phone app saved.

browser.description: The browser app uses Web Bluetooth. It works in a browser that supports Web Bluetooth, such as Chrome.

topic.lockout.title: Lockout
topic.lockout.description: A locked board does not keep a change from the app. The app shows the lock state of the board on the device screen. Unlock the board with its LOCKOUT button.
